content.title: Chuck Norris movies with the highest ratings, according to IMDb
content.text: (WOWK) – Actor and martial artist Chuck Norris has died at the age of 86, according to his family. The Norris family released a statement Friday morning saying that Chuck Norris passed away Thursday morning. On Thursday, TMZ had reported that Norris was training on the Hawaiian island of Kauai when he suffered a medical emergency, but sources for the outlet claimed he was “in good spirits.” Norris was born Carlos Ray Norris in Ryan, Oklahoma, on March 10, 1940. He became successful in competitive martial arts and was a six-time undefeated World Professional Middleweight Karate champion. He even went on to found his own Korean-based American hard style of karate known sometimes as Chun Kuk Do and the United Fighting Arts Federation. In 1968, Norris made his film debut in “The Wrecking Crew” as an uncredited bodyguard. In martial arts circles, he met and befriended Bruce Lee, leading to their iconic fight scene in the 1972 film “Return of the Dragon,” also known as “The Way of the Dragon.” Thanks to his martial arts skills and the tough-guy characters he often played, Norris became something of a meme in the mid-2000s after a series of silly, extremely hyperbolic “facts” about him began going viral online. In honor of Norris’ long and iconic career, here are his five top-rated films per IMDb. 5: “Code of Silence” – 6.1 on IMDb and 68% on Rotten Tomatoes This 1985 film stars Norris as Eddie Cusack, a Chicago police officer caught in the middle of a gang war. He becomes shunned by his colleagues when he refuses to help cover up for an officer who planted a gun on an innocent bystander during a gunfire exchange. Other top-billed actors include Henry Silva, Bert Remsen, Mike Genovese, Molly Hagan and Nathan Davis. 4: “Lone Wolfe McQuade” – 6.3 on IMDb and 57% on Rotten Tomatoes This 1983 film stars Norris as J.J. McQuade, a Texas Ranger who prefers working alone. The film begins with McQuade helping Texas authorities during a gun battle with bandits. After his commanding officer insists he take a partner, McQuade ends up on the trail of an arms dealer and drug lord. Other top-billed actors include David Carradine, Barbara Carrera, Leon Isaac Kennedy, Robert Beltran and Dana Kimmell as McQuade’s daughter Sally. 3: “The Expendables 2” 6.6 on IMDb and 68% on Rotten Tomatoes This 2012 film is a sequel to the 2010 film, “The Expendables,” which is about a CIA operative who hires a team of mercenaries for a mission. This second film sends the characters on a quest for revenge in enemy territory. Norris plays the role of retired military operative Booker, a nod to his character John T. Booker in the 1978 film “Good Guys Wear Black,” and another character refers to Booker as “Lone Wolf,” which is a nod to his 1983 film “Lone Wolf McQuade.” This was Norris’ final film role, according to IMDb. 2: “Dodgeball: A True Underdog Story” – 6.7 on IMDb and 72% on Rotten Tomatoes This 2004 slapstick comedy features a group of “misfits” who enter a dodgeball tournament in Las Vegas with the goal of saving their local gym. Some of the top-billed cast are Vince Vaughn, Ben Stiller, Rip Torn and Christine Taylor. Norris’ role in the film is a cameo as himself, as a member of the dodgeball judiciary board. Lance Armstrong and David Hasselhoff also have cameo appearances in the movie. 1: “The Way of the Dragon” – 7.1 on IMDb and 87% on Rotten Tomatoes This 1972 Bruce Lee film, which was originally released as “Return of the Dragon” in the United States, was Norris’ first credited film role. According to IMDb, the film follows a “country bumpkin” martial artist who goes to Rome to help relatives who are being harassed by gangsters. Norris plays Colt, a martial artist hired to challenge Lee’s character, Tang Lung, leading to the well-known fight scene between Norris and Lee. Honorable Mention: “Walker, Texas Ranger” – 5.7 on IMDb and no Rotten Tomatoes rating While not a film role, we cannot end the list without an honorable mention to Norris’ leading role in the television series “Walker, Texas Ranger.” The series ran from 1993 to 2001, and starred Norris as Cordell Walker, a Texas Ranger who, along with partner James Trivette, played by Clarence Gilyard, Jr., battled crime in Dallas and across the Lone Star State. Nexstar Media Group, Inc.’s Michael Bartiromo contributed to this report.
